scope: Phase1 current source to Shared OCP/ROSA portability assessment for P2 topology decision

items.rationale: Application code uses HTTP/PostgreSQL and environment-injected DATABASE_URL/FDS_ENGINE_URL; no AWS/ROSA SDK dependency observed.
items.action: Retain same image/business contract. Validate image supports OpenShift arbitrary UID before declaring runtime portability.

items.rationale: apps/v1 Deployment, v1 Service, probes, resources, emptyDir and standard pod security fields are Kubernetes APIs.
items.action: Create one authoritative portable workload base; existing fds-msa files are reference snapshots and infra-kubernetes manifest is a security patch/reference rather than the Phase2 deployment source.

items.rationale: Current manifests explicitly request runAsUser 10001 and runAsGroup 999/10001. OpenShift restricted-v2 constrains explicit UID to the project/SCC allowed range.
items.action: Do not grant a broader/custom SCC just to preserve fixed IDs. First test arbitrary-UID compatibility; prefer removing fixed UID/GID from OpenShift overlay while retaining runAsNonRoot, seccomp RuntimeDefault, readOnlyRootFilesystem and drop ALL if image permissions permit.

items.rationale: Phase1 uses NodePort 30080 + edge01 reverse proxy. ROSA/OpenShift P2 expects Route-based health/access and managed ingress.
items.action: Portable base should keep ClusterIP service. Put OpenShift Route/TLS/ingress exposure in a ROSA/OpenShift overlay.

items.rationale: Namespace PSA labels are pinned to Kubernetes v1.36 based on Phase1 runtime. ROSA/OpenShift cluster version can differ and SCC also participates in admission.
items.action: Do not carry v1.36 labels verbatim. Derive supported PSA version or use target-compatible labels after ROSA version freeze; preserve restricted intent.

items.rationale: networking.k8s.io/v1 is portable, but edge01/db01/monitor01/control-plane/worker IP blocks are Phase1 topology values.
items.action: Split policy intent from environment endpoints. Keep pod/namespace selector rules in base; inject approved DB/monitoring/source CIDRs and validate OVN-Kubernetes semantics with negative tests.

items.rationale: Core RBAC APIs and no-token service accounts are portable; CI deploy role is already limited to two existing deployments.
items.action: Reuse least-privilege intent. Recreate target-specific short-lived credential/token flow and verify deny cases on ROSA.

items.rationale: Static local PVs bind host paths to k8s-worker03 and kubernetes.io/no-provisioner. They cannot be transplanted to managed ROSA workers as-is.
items.action: For ROSA monitoring, replace with approved CSI-backed StorageClass/PVC (for example EBS-backed storage) via environment overlay. Do not change P0 app topology decision solely for P1 monitoring.

items.rationale: node-exporter design uses hostNetwork, hostPID, hostPort and hostPath, requiring privileged namespace/SCC treatment and managed-platform validation.
items.action: Keep outside P0 topology gate unless monitoring is promoted. Prefer supported OpenShift/ROSA monitoring integration before recreating host-level DaemonSet privileges.

items.rationale: Commit→test→build→scan→digest contract is target-independent, but current workflow is pinned to cicd-runner01 labels/hostname/user and on-prem offline supply paths; current checked workflow does not itself prove ROSA deploy.
items.action: Preserve external Runner and digest traceability. Parameterize target API/namespace/credential/registry and add ROSA deployment adapter without duplicating build/scan logic.

items.rationale: Application endpoint is externalized by env/Secret, which is portable; actual source CIDR, VPN route, SG/NACL and cross-cloud path are AWS/Hybrid environment inputs.
items.action: Keep DATABASE_URL/FDS_ENGINE_URL externalized. Bind ROSA worker source/route/TLS/port through #35/#37/#47 rather than application image.

items.rationale: Both repositories are still initialization-only; no Terraform ROSA module or ROSA manifests exist yet.
items.action: Implement layered boundary: common network/interface -> AWS IAM/OIDC -> topology-specific ROSA provisioning -> cluster platform config -> portable workload. This is a design opportunity, not existing code debt.

PG-01.reason: No single authoritative portable workload base exists yet.

PG-03.reason: Fixed UID/GID requires restricted-v2 compatibility test.

PG-04.reason: Standard NetworkPolicy API but environment IPs and CNI behavior require overlay/runtime validation.

PG-05.reason: P0 app has no persistent workload storage dependency; monitoring local PV is non-portable.

PG-06.reason: Delivery contract reusable, executor/target bindings need adapter.

PG-07.reason: Hybrid interface intent portable; AWS/OCI/on-prem route/source inputs are environment-specific.

PG-09.reason: Evidence contract exists; HCP/Classic target evidence still not runtime-validated.

topology_implication.note: Most current portability risks are common to both HCP and Classic because they arise at OpenShift workload/admission and environment-adapter layers, not control-plane placement.
topology_implication.classic_specific_advantage: Greater customer-account visibility of control-plane/infra architecture, relevant only if host-level/control-plane evidence becomes an approved P0 need.
topology_implication.hcp_specific_risk: Lower customer visibility of control-plane hosts, but no current P0 AC requiring direct control-plane host operations was found.
topology_implication.decision_rule: Do not select Classic solely for structural similarity and do not select HCP solely for cost. Clear PG-01/02/03/08, then compare security/evidence, hybrid path, operability, cost and schedule.
